settled.point: where a whole-number price becomes a Decimal
settled.decided: tax.to_cent reads the amount it rounds by Decimal(amount); Line keeps the price it was given
settled.ground: Rounding to the cent is tax.py's decision, and every stated amount goes through to_cent, so one change there makes render, subtotal, total and tax_of all take a whole number. Decimal() reads an int exactly. Converting in Line instead would change Line.price from 50 to Decimal('50') for code that reads it, which 1.4.0 didn't do.

settled.point: how a second --rate is seen, and the message
settled.decided: --rate uses action="append", and main refuses a list of more than one with parser.error: `argument --rate: the tax rate is given more than once; give it once, such as --rate 19`, also when both rates are the same
settled.ground: argparse otherwise keeps only the last value, so main could never see the first. parser.error is how every other refusal in command.py is made, and it gives the same `invoicer: error: argument --rate:` opening as the other rate refusals. Each value still goes through _rate first, so a wrong value such as 0.19 is named before the repeat is.
